bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.name: Vegetarian Baby Corn and Oyster Mushroom Stir-Fry
aliases: Vegetarian Baby Corn with Oyster Mushrooms
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.serving_basis: One stir-fried side dish to share among four people.
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.description: Crisp, naturally sweet baby corn is stir-fried with tender oyster mushrooms and lightly seasoned with vegetarian oyster sauce and pepper. Serve it hot as an easy everyday vegetable dish.
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.finished_dish: The baby corn is just tender and still crisp, while the mushrooms are soft without turning soggy. A light coating of seasoning leaves little liquid on the plate.
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and finish with scallions and pepper.
tips: Split the baby corn lengthwise so it cooks evenly without a long stir-fry.
Drain the mushrooms well before cooking to keep the dish from becoming watery.
Taste the vegetarian oyster sauce before adding salt, since brands vary in saltiness.
search_terms: vegetarian baby corn and oyster mushroom stir-fry
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian baby corn and oyster mushroom stir-fry with scallions and red chili.
bap-non-xao-nam-bao-ngu-chay.time_note: About 25 minutes; boiling time depends on the size and tenderness of the baby corn.
ingredients: Tear into bite-size pieces, rinse briefly and drain well.
Reduce as needed depending on the sauce.
Add after turning off the heat.
preparation_steps: Rinse the baby corn and split each piece lengthwise. Tear the oyster mushrooms into bite-size pieces, rinse briefly and drain well.
Finely slice the scallions. Set out the vegetarian oyster sauce, seasoning powder, salt and pepper.
cooking_steps: Put the baby corn in a small pot with a splash of water and boil until just tender. Remove and set aside when most of the water has evaporated.
Heat the oil in a pan and stir-fry the mushrooms until softened and lightly browned. Add the baby corn, vegetarian oyster sauce, seasoning powder and salt; toss until evenly coated.
Cook for a few more minutes until the corn is crisp-tender. Taste, turn off the heat and finish with pepper and scallions.

rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.name: Vietnamese Pepper Elder Salad with Tofu
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.serving_basis: One shared salad platter for four people.
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.description: Crisp pepper elder greens leaves are tossed with golden fried tofu and a tangy-sweet lime dressing. This light salad brings a fresh contrast to a vegetarian rice meal.
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.finished_dish: The greens remain bright and crisp, and the tofu is lightly golden outside. The dressing coats the leaves without pooling beneath them.
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.serving: Dress and toss the greens just before serving. Enjoy with steamed rice or as a light starter.
tips: Wash the greens gently and drain them thoroughly so the leaves stay intact and the dressing is not diluted.
Let the tofu cool slightly before tossing it with the greens.
The salad releases moisture after dressing, so mix it only when ready to eat.
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.image_alt: A plate of pepper elder greens salad with golden fried tofu, lime dressing and red chili.
rau-cang-cua-tron-dau-hu.time_note: About 30 minutes, including frying the tofu; toss the greens just before serving.
ingredients: Pick out damaged leaves, rinse and drain thoroughly.
Optional; rinse and tear into bite-size pieces.
Cut into small cubes and pat dry before frying.
For frying the tofu; the amount used depends on the pan.
Finely mince and adjust to taste.
preparation_steps: Rinse the pepper elder greens and lettuce. Soak briefly in lightly salted water, rinse again and drain thoroughly.
Cut the tofu into small cubes and pat dry. Stir together the vegetarian fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and minced chili.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the tofu until lightly golden on all sides. Drain on paper towel and let it cool slightly.
Arrange the greens on a platter. Add just enough dressing and the tofu, then toss gently right before serving.

cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.name: Vegetarian Lotus Root and Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry
aliases: Lotus Root and Vegetarian Ham Stir-Fry
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.serving_basis: One vegetable stir-fry to share among four people.
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.description: Crisp lotus root slices are stir-fried with carrot, bell peppers and vegetarian ham. Soy sauce with a little five-spice powder gives the vegetables a savory finish and a bright look for the family table.
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.finished_dish: The lotus root is tender-crisp and the vegetables keep their shape and natural color. A thin glaze coats the ingredients without making them soft.
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.serving: Serve hot, topped with sliced scallions, alongside steamed rice.
tips: Soak the sliced lotus root in lightly salted water to limit discoloration.
Cut the vegetables to similar sizes so they cook evenly.
Mix the tapioca starch with water separately and add it gradually to control the sauce thickness.
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian lotus root stir-fried with carrot, bell peppers and vegetarian ham.
cu-sen-xao-rau-cu-chay.time_note: About 35 minutes, including preparation, briefly boiling the lotus root and stir-frying the vegetables.
ingredients: Peel and slice about 0.5 cm thick.
Cut into thin slices or flower shapes.
Remove the seeds and cut into bite-size pieces.
Remove the seeds and cut into bite-size pieces.
Choose a plant-based product and cut into bite-size pieces.
Rinse; separate the white and green parts.
Adjust to the saltiness of the soy sauce.
Use a small amount for aroma.
Dissolve in a little water before adding.
preparation_steps: Peel the lotus root, slice it about half a centimeter thick and soak in lightly salted water. Cut the carrot, both bell peppers and vegetarian ham into bite-size pieces.
Mix the soy sauce, vegetarian seasoning, sugar and five-spice powder with about 100 ml of water. Dissolve the tapioca starch separately in a little water.
cooking_steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Briefly boil the lotus root and carrot for about 4–5 minutes until just tender. Drain; plunge briefly into ice water if you want extra crunch, then drain again.
Heat the oil and saute the white part of the scallion until fragrant. Add the bell peppers and stir quickly, then add the lotus root, carrot and vegetarian ham.
Pour in the soy mixture and stir-fry over medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Add the starch slurry a little at a time and toss until the sauce lightly thickens, then turn off the heat.

canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.name: Vegetarian Sweet Leaf and Mushroom Soup
aliases: Sweet Leaf Soup with Straw Mushrooms
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.serving_basis: One bowl of vegetable soup for four people.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.description: Gently bruised sweet leaf greens simmer with straw mushrooms and wood ear in a light broth. The simple combination draws on the natural flavor of the greens and mushrooms without an animal-based stock.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.finished_dish: The broth is clear, the greens are tender but not mushy, and the mushrooms are cooked through with a slight bite from the wood ear.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.serving: Ladle into a bowl and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Bruise the leaves gently so they soften without breaking down.
Add the mushrooms after the greens are tender to keep their texture.
Season the vegetarian fish sauce and seasoning powder gradually because their salt levels vary.
search_terms: sweet-leaf greens soup with straw mushrooms
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.image_alt: A bowl of vegetarian sweet leaf soup with clear broth, leafy greens and mixed mushrooms.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-nam-chay.time_note: About 25 minutes; dried wood ear must be rehydrated before cooking.
ingredients: Pick the leaves, rinse and gently bruise.
Trim the dirty ends and rinse briefly; halve larger mushrooms.
Adjust to the desired amount of broth.
For briefly stir-frying the greens and wood ear.
preparation_steps: Pick through the sweet leaf greens, discarding old or damaged leaves. Rinse and gently bruise them. Rehydrate the dried wood ear and slice it; clean the straw mushrooms.
Measure out the vegetarian fish sauce, seasoning powder and water. Halve larger straw mushrooms so they cook evenly.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and briefly stir-fry the sweet leaf greens and wood ear. Season with vegetarian fish sauce and seasoning powder; cook for about 3–5 minutes until the greens soften.
Add the water and bring the soup to a boil. Skim if needed, add the straw mushrooms and simmer for about 4–5 minutes until the greens and mushrooms are just cooked.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, turn off the heat and ladle the soup into a bowl.

nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.name: Vegetarian Oyster Mushrooms Braised with Lemongrass and Chili
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.serving_basis: One platter of braised mushrooms to share among four people.
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.description: Torn oyster mushrooms are braised with lemongrass, ginger, garlic and chili in soy sauce. As the liquid reduces to a light glaze, the mushrooms become tender and aromatic, ready to serve with steamed rice.
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.finished_dish: The mushroom pieces are tender but retain their fibers, coated in a soy-brown glaze with a bright lemongrass and ginger aroma.
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, garnished with scallions and pepper.
tips: Tear the mushrooms along their fibers and drain them well so they take up seasoning without releasing too much water.
Braise over low heat and stir gently while liquid remains to keep the mushrooms intact.
Taste the soy sauce before adding salt because brands vary in saltiness.
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian oyster mushrooms braised in soy sauce with lemongrass, scallions and pepper.
nam-bao-ngu-kho-sa-ot-chay.time_note: About 40 minutes, including mushroom preparation, sauteing the aromatics and reducing the braising liquid.
ingredients: Tear into pieces along the fibers, rinse quickly and drain well.
Finely mince the tender lower part; reserve a few thin slices if desired.
Choose a product suitable for vegetarian cooking.
For a brown color; reduce if the product is salty.
Add only if needed after tasting the sauce.
preparation_steps: Tear the oyster mushrooms into bite-size pieces, rinse quickly and drain thoroughly. Mince the lemongrass, ginger and garlic; slice the chili and scallions.
Stir the soy sauce, caramel coloring and water together. Taste it before adding salt.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot. Saute the lemongrass, ginger and garlic until fragrant, then add the mushrooms and toss gently until they begin to soften.
Add the soy mixture, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and braise until the mushrooms are tender and the liquid has reduced to a light glossy coating.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add chili and pepper to taste, scatter over the scallions and turn off the heat.
